title: Session rotation exposes transient SAML group TTL mismatch causing ghost admin access and intermittent denies
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Customer escalation: multiple enterprise customers reported two related behaviors after enabling RBAC v2 with SAML provisioning + session token rotation: (1) users intermittently retained admin-level privileges after their SAML group membership was removed (ghost admin access), and (2) other users were temporarily denied access immediately after an identity provider (IdP) session refresh even though their SAML assertion included the correct groups.

Observed behavior (concrete):
- Customer A: User U1 removed from 'admins' group in IdP. Within 30–120s they could still access admin console routes and perform admin actions; audit logs showed those actions attributed to U1 but without a clear link to the original SAML assertion change.
- Customer B: User U2 performed an SSO re-auth (IdP rotated session token). Immediately after re-auth they received 403 on previously accessible resources for 10–90s until the next reconciliation job.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Configure RBAC v2 with SAML SSO for a test org; set session token TTL to 1h and enable SAML group provisioning.
2) Log in as a user with 'admins' group -> verify admin access.
3) From IdP, remove user from 'admins' group and trigger a SSO re-issue (rotate assertion) for the session.
4) Observe: sometimes RBAC v2 still enforces admin role for existing session for ~1–2 minutes (ghost). Alternatively, rotate token for another user and observe immediate 403 until reconciliation job runs.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by trace logs & local repro):
- Two TTLs are out of sync: (A) session token TTL (long, e.g., 3600s) and (B) transient SAML group claim cache TTL / role binding reconciliation window (short, e.g., 30s).
- When the IdP re-issues an assertion with a new NameID/Subject or when group assertions expire on the IdP side, the RBAC v2 binding cache sometimes keeps the old role grants until either the cache entry expires or the reconciliation job runs.
- In some flows the subject identifier emitted by the IdP changed on rotation (NameID vs. eduPersonPrincipalName), causing RBAC to create a second identity mapping and not correctly link prior audit events. This split identity explains missing/fragmented audit entries.
- Delegated admin binding logic had a subtle bug: elevated bindings created by 'delegated_admin' flow were stored with a stale session_subject reference and did not get invalidated when group claims changed, allowing ghost admin actions to succeed for a short time.

Why this is customer-impacting and high priority:
- Unauthorized admin actions during the ghost window are real security incidents.
- Fragmented audit trails prevent customers and SRE from determining whether an action should have been allowed at the time, complicating incident response and compliance audits.

Mitigation implemented (prod fast-follow):
- Rolled out a short-term server-side mitigation (2025-02-12): on session rotation events we now proactively enqueue an immediate reconciliation job for the session subject to re-evaluate claims and apply/remove role bindings synchronously for the next 10s. This reduced customer complaints but is not a robust long-term fix.

Planned long-term fixes (this ticket):
1) Canonical subject mapping: normalize and persist a stable identifier (prefer NameID if stable, fallback to configured stable claim). Add migration to backfill alternate_id mappings for existing sessions.
2) Claim-binding TTL alignment: remove the independent short TTL for cached SAML group claims and tie claim validity to session token lifecycle or use a soft-expiry + active-recheck on certain events (session rotation, API key change).
3) Atomic reconcile on session claims change: when we detect a changed assertion, perform an atomic rebind of roles (compute diff, apply remove/add with audit audit-entries linking old_session_id -> new_session_id).
4) Delegated-admin fix: ensure delegated admin role bindings reference canonical identity and include a revocation hook triggered by claim changes.
5) Audit enhancement: include prior_subject_id and session_rotation_id in audit events and add a reconciliation log entry when role bindings change as a result of claim refresh so replayable evidence exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- No ghost admin access window > 5s in controlled repro.
- Immediate reconciliation on session rotation reduces customer 403/overgrant complaints to nil in canary orgs.
- Audit logs for reconciliations include prior_subject_id and session_rotation_id; cross-org queries show continuous trails.
- E2E tests added to RBAC integration harness that simulate NameID changes, transient group drop, and delegated admin revoke flows.

Rollout plan:
- Implementation in feature branch -> unit/integration tests -> deploy to canary (internal + 2 customer orgs) -> monitor for 48h -> staged rollout to rest of hosts.
- Monitoring: add reconciliation latency dashboard, metric for "reconciliations triggered by session rotation", and a histogram for "time delta between IdP claim change and RBAC role removal".

Customer communication:
- Ops sent interim note (2025-02-13) to affected customers describing mitigation and ETA for permanent fix. Will follow up with postmortem and audit reconciliation details once migration finishes.
comments: 2025-02-11 Diego Morales: Confirmed reproduction in staging using SAML test IdP. Observed Subject(NameID) changed after IdP refresh in 30% of flows. Attaching logs to PR.
2025-02-12 Ava Chen: Deployed short-term enqueue-on-rotation mitigation (hotfix). Initial reduction in reports; still seeing 5–20s windows in edge cases.

2025-02-14 Priya Natarajan (Security): Reviewed planned audit schema changes. Approved adding prior_subject_id and session_rotation_id fields; requested data retention and access controls be documented.

2025-02-17 Diego Morales: Implemented canonical subject mapping prototype. Need review: GH PR #5421. Notable trade-off: choosing canonical claim requires org-level override setting to support IdPs with non-standard NameID semantics.
2025-02-19 QA: Added integration tests for delegated-admin revoke flow. One flaky test failing on CI due to timing; increased reconciliation timeout to 5s and re-ran.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical subject resolver. Integration tests that run full reconciliation flow for: (a) NameID change, (b) group removal while session still valid, (c) delegated-admin creation + group removal. Add e2e harness scenario to run nightly against staging IdP. Canary deployment to two customers for 48h. Metrics: reconciliation duration, number of immediate reconciliations triggered, audit continuity score.
resolution: incomplete - mitigation deployed; long-term fixes in development
next_steps: 1) Finalize canonical subject selection implementation and config (owner: Diego) 2) Implement atomic reconciliation and audit linkage (owner: Diego) 3) Add migration to backfill alternate_id mappings (owner: infra-team) 4) Schedule security review for audit schema changes (owner: Priya) 5) Canary rollout and monitoring (owner: SRE)
postmortem_todo: After rollout, generate customer-facing postmortem with timeline, root cause, and audit reconciliation. Provide customers with consolidated audit export for the affected time window on request.
